# L1 Code macOS patch

Upstream is the official `tauri-plugin-notification` crate 2.3.3, published from `tauri-apps/plugins-workspace` commit `e7a68fa63755603b9fa12d28e077eea645551d24`, directory `plugins/notification`. Source came from the crates.io release archive. MIT and Apache-2.0 license notices are retained. Packaged screenshots, JavaScript build sources and test artifacts are omitted; the compiled initialization scripts, plugin build inputs, permissions and platform source are retained.

L1 Code selects `src/macos.rs` instead of the official `desktop.rs` on macOS. The official backend reports permission granted without asking macOS, ignores action metadata and uses Terminal's identity in development. The replacement uses Apple's UserNotifications framework behind the same notification plugin commands. Permission and delivery commands await Apple completion handlers without blocking the main thread. The Rust `on_action` and `NotificationData::extra` extensions carry clicked-notification metadata to L1 Code. The Rust `remove_delivered` extension removes delivered notifications by request identifier, which is the notification `group`, so L1 Code can close a thread's alert as T3 closes pending notifications. The synchronous Rust builder reports asynchronous delivery failures through `notification:delivery-error`; L1 Code awaits the plugin `notify` command instead.

The delegate stays retained for the plugin lifetime. UserInfo contains the serialized notification data. L1 Code validates thread targets before navigation and queues click targets until its renderer listener is ready. Native dispatch has no OS sound. T3 audio owns notification sound. `willPresent` suppresses native alerts while the app is foreground. Permission is requested only from the explicit General dropdown action. It asks for alert and badge authorization, as Electron does for T3, because an app authorized for alerts alone did not show its dock badge on macOS. Unbundled development executables return an unavailable error without assuming Terminal's identity.

This maintained backend patch supports L1 Code's immediate title/body/group/extra notification subset. It does not add desktop implementations of the official mobile scheduling, channel or action registration commands. Windows and Linux retain the official backend; L1 Code's native click extension currently supports macOS. Rebase the backend selection and async commands when updating the upstream crate, then verify permission, silent delivery and clicks in an actual bundled app.

Native dependency license metadata was read from the locked crate manifests. `objc2` 0.6.4, `objc2-foundation` 0.3.2 and `block2` 0.6.2 are MIT. `objc2-user-notifications` 0.3.2 is Zlib OR Apache-2.0 OR MIT. `futures-channel` 0.3.34 is MIT OR Apache-2.0.

T3 notification components in `src` come from `pingdotgg/t3code` v0.0.45, commit `6c8fed35d`, under MIT. The source components have one-line source headers. The MP3 assets `src/assets/notification-completion.mp3` and `notification-input.mp3` are byte-identical to T3's copies (SHA-256 `910311c1…` and `57089914…`). T3 records them as derivatives of deadrobotmusic's freesound sounds 750607 and 750609, dedicated to the public domain under CC0-1.0, not MIT. `third-party-licenses.config.json` carries their notices.
